title: Compact journey map with rollout-stage lenses
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact information architecture for the Redwood Console that unifies workspace switching, primary navigation, and rollout telemetry into a small footprint 'journey map'. The goal is to reduce vertical real estate usage while surfacing rollout stage lenses (canary, gradual, full) and a cost overview without forcing users into deep drill-downs. This ticket covers concept exploration, mid-fidelity prototype, and a first round of stakeholder reviews with PM/Eng and Design Ops.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates workspace switch + route discovery in <=2 clicks for primary workflows
Rollout-stage lenses visually indicate status and provide a one-click drill to rollout detail view
Cost lens surfaces top 3 contributors (model, route, timeframe) inline within the map
Interaction patterns validated with 6 internal stakeholders and updated based on feedback
Handoff artifacts (Figma frames, tokens, interaction spec) uploaded and linked to PRD
comments: 2026-01-20 - Initial sketch review with PM (Ravi Singh). PM requested explicit 'safety fallback' affordance for canary failures.
2026-01-27 - Scoped prototype to include cost-lens summary (top 3 cost drivers) instead of full cost detail to preserve compactness.
2026-02-05 - Engineering sync (Elena Torres) flagged KV cache telemetry limitations; we added a lightweight telemetry badge rather than full traces.
2026-02-18 - Mid-fidelity prototype uploaded to Figma. Design Ops requested tokens and spacing spec for parity across consoles.
2026-02-26 - Usability session #1 (6 participants): discoverability of rollout lenses was lower than expected — adjusted contrast and microcopy for states.
2026-03-02 - Accessibility review: ensured 4.5:1 contrast for status chips and added keyboard focus flows for workspace switcher.
2026-03-08 - PM review: Ravi approved the information hierarchy; asked to add 'cost trend sparkline' for last 24h in the lens.
2026-03-10 - Submitted design handoff package and PR to console-prototypes repo. Awaiting ENG-9182 feasibility review for runtime data endpoints.
decisions: Use a persistent condensed left 'journey map' rail (40px compact, expands on hover) to balance screen real estate and route discoverability
Surface rollout-stage lenses as stacked chips with color-coded health + microcopy rather than full tiles to keep the surface compact
Include inline cost-lens summary (3 contributors + 24h sparkline) in the journey map rather than a separate cost panel to reduce context switches
Defer full per-token cost breakdown to the detailed cost view; this prototype focuses on quick triage signals
Keyboard-first interactions required: workspace switcher and runway actions reachable in <=3 keystrokes
next_steps: ENG-9182: confirm runtime endpoints for rollout status and cost-summaries (blocking)
Finalize microcopy for rollout states and confirm translations with localization team
Run 2 additional usability sessions focused on newcomers (non-console frequent users)
Create engineering tickets for interactive states: hover expansion, keyboard nav, and ARIA labels
Schedule design-review with Platform Reliability to validate telemetry surface doesn't leak sensitive data
